articles.title: Agentic World Action Models
articles.summary: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. articles.title: When to retire: the cultural evolution of post-reproductive oblique teaching
articles.summary: Teaching is ubiquitous across human societies. Instruction from parents to offspring is the most fundamental form of teaching, explained primarily through kin selection and inclusive fitness. Instruction to non-kin, known as oblique teaching, also plays a dominant role in modern societies, where teaching is often institutionalized. articles.title: A signature of the timelike singularity in holography
articles.summary: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, we provide a simple observable, the imaginary part of the retarded Green's function, which captures the timelike singularity of a charged black brane. articles.title: Optimal galaxy magnification: generalized fundamental-plane residuals and number counts are all you need
articles.summary: Weak-lensing magnification complements cosmic shear through its effects on galaxy fluxes, sizes, and number counts. We derive the optimal magnification statistics from galaxy properties and show that the optimal measurement can be decomposed into an optimal mean statistic and total number counts. articles.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
articles.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. articles.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
articles.summary: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. articles.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
articles.summary: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. articles.title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
articles.summary: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. articles.title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
articles.summary: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity, with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating operator product coefficients. Our construction starts from compact regions assembled from generalized hyperbolic tetrahedra. articles.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
articles.summary: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. articles.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
articles.summary: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. articles.title: Geometric Algebra for Neural Networks: A Survey
articles.summary: Geometric algebra (GA) unifies geometric primitives and transformations in a single algebraic framework. Neural networks designed around this framework often represent features as multivectors and constrain layer operations to respect the algebraic structure, enabling principled treatment of geometric transformations and, in many cases, built-in equivariance. articles.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
articles.summary: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. We argue that their visual foundation should combine physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction, so that a single representation can support prediction, instruction, and inspection. articles.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks
articles.summary: The success of convolutional neural networks is often attributed to locality and weight sharing. However, how these two properties separately shape learning, and how their effects depend on the spatial correlations of natural images, remain poorly understood. articles.title: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
articles.summary: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. articles.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
articles.summary: Through a tangle of real-world interactions, from synthetic training pipelines to data shared on the open web, frontier LLMs absorb what their predecessors and competitors create. How well does each model play its role in this ecosystem, as a creator and as a solver? We introduce Environment Duels, a dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates both capabilities on interactive environments. articles.title: Predictions for an unseen third planet in the WISPIT 2 system
articles.summary: We predict the mass and semi-major axis of a currently unseen but hypothesised planet in the WISPIT 2 system based on the location of the ring observed by ALMA at 144.4 au. Using findings from previous hydrodynamical models, we predict that a ~0.2-1 $M_{Jup}$ planet may exist at ~ 100-120 au. articles.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
articles.summary: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period. articles.title: Technical Report: Causal ANOVA Applied to COMPAS
articles.summary: This report applies Causal ANOVA to the COMPAS recidivism prediction dataset to study how demographic variables contribute to variation in two-year recidivism outcomes. Using a directed acyclic graph (DAG) to encode causal assumptions, we estimate counterfactual explainability scores for Race, Sex, and Age Category. articles.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
articles.summary: We analyze the problem of estimating univariate Gaussian mixture densities using the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) based on $n$ independent and identically distributed samples. articles.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
articles.summary: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. articles.title: On Particle Production from Bubble Collisions in the Non-runaway Regime
articles.summary: Particle production from bubble collisions during First-Order Phase Transitions (FOPTs) has been studied as an efficient mechanism for baryogenesis and dark matter production, but existing semi-analytical treatments assume runaway bubbles with wall velocity $v_w\to 1$. articles.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
articles.summary: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. articles.summary: Many NP-complete (NPC) problems have a polynomial-time (P) twin that differs in a single structural detail, such as 3- versus 2-colouring a graph. articles.summary: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems must maintain efficient and safe energy delivery under variations in geometry, coupling, load, alignment, and operating conditions. articles.summary: Query rewriting and semantic evaluation of text-to-SQL systems both depend on deciding whether two SQL queries return the same result on every database satisfying the schema constraints. articles.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) has become a central paradigm for aligning Large Language Models with human values. However, the reliance on sensitive preference data necessitates rigorous differential privacy (DP) guarantees to prevent user information leakage. articles.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. articles.summary: Aims: This study aims to place constraints on the spin of Sgr A* from recent flare observations. articles.summary: We study the response of compressible microtubule-based active fluids to sinusoidally varying activity patterns, using experiments and theory. articles.title: An Implicit Conservative Finite Volume Scheme with Poisson Brackets for the Steady-State Transport of Galactic Cosmic Rays
articles.summary: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) pose a persistent radiation hazard to astronauts and spacecraft in the heliosphere. Modeling their transport is essential for understanding how the solar wind and heliospheric magnetic field shape their spatial distributions and energy spectra. articles.summary: Perimeter triage faces a latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and produce unparseable output. articles.summary: Today's multimodal assistants are typically prompted to interpret the visual evidence presented to them. To offload the cognitive burden of remembering across long horizons, wearable assistants should instead proactively acquire and maintain useful memory as the user's surroundings evolve. articles.title: Orbitol: Crystal Generation on Wyckoff Orbits
articles.summary: Generative models propose crystalline materials by learning composition and geometry, but unconditional sampling gives no direct control over the space group, which constrains whether responses such as piezoelectricity are symmetry-allowed. articles.summary: A species-resolved anisotropy-response scaling framework is used to investigate heavy-quark dynamics through the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) azimuthal anisotropies of $D^0$ mesons. articles.summary: Standardizing variables by their sample standard deviations is routine in multivariate analysis and removes marginal scale differences before dependence is assessed. articles.summary: We study what happens to RMSProp when the learning rate is too large for convergence to the minimizer. articles.title: Circuits of LLM Classifiers
articles.summary: Language models make it easy to build classifiers by simply prompting a model with the sample to classify. However, their predictions are neither deterministic nor uniformly reliable across samples. How can we combine predictions from different models to improve reliability? articles.title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
articles.summary: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. articles.title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
articles.summary: Data agents built on ReAct-style loops now execute complex analytical workflows over structured data, yet their intermediate reasoning still runs almost entirely through text. Human analysts instead move between numbers, tables, and charts, reading visual evidence to expose trends and anomalies that text summaries drop. articles.title: A random sampling method to test the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
articles.summary: We introduce a random sampling method for testing the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (wETH) that is particularly useful for large, sparse Hamiltonians. articles.title: Loopholing All the Way: Language Modeling with pure Self-Conditioning
articles.summary: Recent Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) use Self-Conditioning (SC), or Loopholing, to improve their performance. articles.title: GoiBERT: Compact Vietnamese Language Models via Two-Stage Knowledge Distillation
articles.summary: Vietnamese pre-trained encoders have improved rapidly, but the strongest ones are large, multilingual-vocabulary models or depend on external word segmentation, which makes them costly to deploy. We present GoiBERT, a family of two compact Vietnamese encoders with 26M and 49M parameters that operate directly on raw text. GoiBERT learns from two complementary teachers. articles.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
articles.summary: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised. During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context. articles.title: Validating Autoformalized Specifications via Contrapuntal Languages
articles.summary: Formal specifications can make AI-generated code mechanically checkable.
